interpreter: agent-led interpretation (Claude) of the 0.5 m pit-free CHM and the 2025-06-14 and 2021-04-18 RGBI photos at their native 0.16 m (colour infrared and natural colour), each photo moved onto the canopy by its window relief displacement; not a survey and not human approval. Windows carried from rounds 1-4 keep their crown interpretation verbatim (copied from reference-annotations-r4.json).
protocol: A reference crown is a tree whose crown is visible in the 2025 photo or the 2021 leaf-off photo AND has laser height support (a CHM blob or apex of at least 2 m). Its position is the interpreted crown centre on the laser (CHM) surface: the apex for a conical crown, the centre of the CHM blob for a broad or flat-topped crown. Photos are displaced by relief and only confirm and classify.
'from' lists the numbered candidate apexes that belong to one crown (the tallest gives the position); 'at' gives an explicit crown centre in metres east/north of the window's south-west corner.
type: conifer when dark green in the April 2021 photo and dark red in the 2025 CIR; broadleaf when bare grey in April 2021 and bright pink in CIR; unknown otherwise.
stratum: isolated (clear of other crowns), group (a small group of touching crowns in the open), edge (outer row of a stand), closed (inside a stand or clump, neighbours on most sides).

ambiguous boxes cover canopy whose crowns cannot be separated with confidence; neither references nor predictions inside them are scored. Crowns in the 6 m margin outside the window are listed so edge predictions can match them; they are not scored.

Round 3: the photos are drawn at their native 0.16 m and moved onto the canopy: each window's relief displacement k (relief.mjs: the photo correlated with a hillshade of the CHM lit from the flight's sun) times its 80th-percentile canopy height. Without it a 20 m crown sits 6-14 m from its laser crown in these flights.

Round 3, crowns: a numbered candidate within about 2 m of a taller one, or less than about 0.6 m above the dip toward a taller one within 3 m, was read as part of that crown unless the photos showed two crowns; for leafless broadleaf crowns, which carry several tops, up to about 3-4 m. Young regrowth and thickets whose stems cannot be told apart are ambiguity boxes. Margin crowns (6 m outside the window) are listed by that rule only, to absorb edge predictions.

Round 3, pine and spruce: each conifer the interpreter could call is marked subtype pine or spruce from chips of both photos at the crown's displaced position (spruce: dark, dense, pointed and regular, green to the ground in the oblique view; pine: lighter and yellower, loose clumpy crown high on a bare stem, a lollipop shadow); conifers the chips did not decide carry no subtype. This reads the same photos a classifier may use; it is not a field identification.

Round 4 (W1-W5, frozen before the photo detector ran anywhere): each window was first drafted by the round-3 rule written above (tools/tree-pipeline/photo/reference-draft.mjs: a numbered candidate within 2 m of a taller kept one, or less than 0.6 m above the dip toward a taller kept one within 3 m, is part of that crown; for a crown leafless in April 2021 within 3.5 m), with a type from the April 2021 vegetated share at the crown displaced position (>= 0.5 conifer, < 0.2 broadleaf, else unknown) and a stratum from the detect census rule (share of CHM >= 3 m in a 16 m square). The interpreter then checked every window on large single panels at 0.06 m (CHM hillshade, June 2025 natural colour and colour infrared, April 2021 natural colour, each photo moved onto the canopy) and changed what the panels contradicted; the changes are in each crown note. No detector output was looked at.

Round 4 limitation: in closed stands the reference reads the same June 2025 photo the round-4 photo detector reads (and the same laser the laser detectors read), so where touching crowns share one laser maximum and one photo blob the split is a judgement that may favour the photo detector. A field check of W1 and W2 would settle it.

Round 4: a tree felled after the 2021 laser (logs on the ground in June 2025, as in W3) remains a reference crown when the April 2021 photo and the laser show it, by the first rule above; the scores are for the 2021 canopy the laser measured.

Round 4b (X1-X5, frozen before any round-4b code ran): each window was first drafted by the round-3 rule written above (tools/tree-pipeline/photo/reference-draft.mjs: a numbered candidate within 2 m of a taller kept one, or less than 0.6 m above the dip toward a taller kept one within 3 m, is part of that crown; for a crown leafless in April 2021 within 3.5 m), with a type from the April 2021 vegetated share at the crown displaced position (>= 0.5 conifer, < 0.2 broadleaf, else unknown) and a stratum from the detect census rule (share of CHM >= 3 m in a 16 m square). The interpreter then checked every window on large single panels at 0.06 m (CHM hillshade, June 2025 natural colour and colour infrared, April 2021 natural colour, each photo moved onto the canopy) and changed what the panels contradicted; the changes are in each crown note. No detector output was looked at.

Round 4 limitation: in closed stands the reference reads the same June 2025 photo the round-4 photo detector reads (and the same laser the laser detectors read), so where touching crowns share one laser maximum and one photo blob the split is a judgement that may favour the photo detector. A field check of X1 and X2 would settle it.

Round 4: a tree felled after the 2021 laser (logs on the ground in June 2025) remains a reference crown when the April 2021 photo and the laser show it, by the first rule above; the scores are for the 2021 canopy the laser measured.
